entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Konrad von Marburg was a medieval German Catholic priest and inquisitor who played a crucial role in Elizabeth of Hungary's life, serving as her spiritual director until her death in 1231. Born into a noble family, von Marburg's early life and education are not well-documented, but his later career as a priest and inquisitor reflects his deep commitment to the Catholic Church. Von Marburg's significance extends beyond his individual achievements, as he was instrumental in shaping the religious and spiritual landscape of medieval Europe.


Konrad von Marburg's influence can be seen in the establishment of the Order of the Golden Fleece, a chivalric order founded by Emperor Frederick II in 1198, which von Marburg helped to promote through his connections with the Holy Roman Emperor.


Von Marburg's legacy can also be seen in the numerous theological treatises and sermons he composed, which continue to be studied by scholars today for their insight into the theology of the time.


In 1233, von Marburg died at the age of 100, leaving behind a legacy that continued to shape the course of European history for centuries to come.
